title: Usage metric access policy delegation and query sanitizer for exports
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Several console analytics endpoints and CSV/JSON export jobs currently rely on coarse-grained RBAC checks that allow users with view access to query arbitrary metric dimensions. This causes two issues: (1) customers with tenant-scoped roles can still craft queries that leak other tenants' aggregates via rollups and joins; (2) cost-sensitive metrics and PII-derived dimensions are accessible too broadly, exposing potential compliance risk.

Goal: Implement an access delegation layer and a query sanitizer that enforces attribute-level entitlements for analytics APIs and long-running export pipelines. The solution must be performant for ad-hoc dashboards and safe for bulk exports (scheduled jobs), preserve existing SLOs, and be compatible with Dedicated/Private deployments where a local entitlement store may be present.
acceptance_criteria:
- All analytics REST endpoints that accept free-form metric queries must pass through the new Policy Delegator before execution.
- Query sanitizer must rewrite or reject queries that reference dimensions or metrics the caller is not entitled to; sanitized queries must not return masked columns.
- Exports (CSV/JSON) created by scheduled jobs must be gated by the same policy and produce audit logs listing which entitlements were applied.
- Unit and integration test coverage demonstrating enforcement for at least: tenant-scoped role, org-admin, billing-only role, and a read-only support role.
- No >5% regression in median query latency on our staging workload compared to baseline.
- Feature guarded behind toggle 'analytics.policy_delegator_v2' for safe rollout.
technical_notes:
Design decisions: hybrid RBAC+ABAC model. Roles remain first-class (org-admin, org-reader, billing, support) while per-metric entitlements are expressed as attributes attached to tokens/identities (metric:cost_sensitive=true, dimension:prism_customer_id=pii).

Enforcement surface: two layers. (A) Policy Delegator service: lightweight HTTP validation service that returns allowed metric/dimension lists and masks. (B) Query Sanitizer middleware in the analytics query gateway that performs AST-level rewrites to remove unauthorized projections and inject tenant filters.

Performance: we will cache delegation responses in an in-memory LRU keyed by (principal_id, project_id, policy_version) with TTL 60s. For exports the scheduler will fetch a signed policy snapshot and attach it to the job payload to avoid repeated calls at runtime.

DB changes: small 'metric_entitlements' table to map entitlement ids to metric patterns for admin UI, plus audit table 'analytics_policy_audits'. Migrations included in PR.

Trade-offs considered: full ABAC would offer fine-grained control but add latency; policy snapshots for exports increase storage but avoid runtime latency spikes. Chosen hybrid reduces changes to client roles and keeps most checks cheap.
implementation_plan:
1) Add metric_entitlements schema and migration (ENG-402317/schema-migration).
2) Implement Policy Delegator service (Go) with endpoints: GET /v1/allowed?principal=... and POST /v1/validate (for batch jobs). Unit tests and contract tests. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-delegator/pull/12)
3) Add query-sanitizer middleware to analytics-gateway that accepts AST, applies allowlist/mask rules, rewrites projections or returns 403. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics-gateway/pull/234)
4) Wire scheduler to fetch policy snapshots for scheduled exports; attach snapshot id to job metadata. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics-scheduler/pull/45)
5) Update console backend endpoints to call delegator and surface error messages. Update SDK docs.
6) End-to-end tests and staging rollout behind feature flag.

Estimated sprint breakdown: schema + delegator core (2), middleware + integration (2), docs + rollout (1).
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for delegator: principal->allowed metrics mapping, cache eviction behavior.
- Integration tests: analytics-gateway + delegator running in docker-compose; include negative tests rejecting unauthorized projections and positive tests allowing permitted views.
- Load test: run typical staging query mix for 30 minutes with flag enabled; measure 95th/median latency and compare to baseline.
- Security review: run static analysis on delegator service and review audit log content for PII redaction.
- Manual verification: create sample roles and queries in staging, export CSV, verify audit row created and no unauthorized columns present.
rollout_plan:
- Feature disabled by default.
- Step 1: Deploy Policy Delegator to canary namespace with read-only mode that logs but does not block. Run for 48 hours and review logs.
- Step 2: Enable blocking for 10% of traffic (random sampling) for 24 hours; monitor errors and query latency.
- Step 3: Increase to 50% for 24 hours, then 100% behind 'analytics.policy_delegator_v2'.
- Step 4: For scheduled exports, require snapshot attachment; old jobs continue to use legacy export path until migration window ends (2 weeks).
- Rollback criteria: >1% increase in 5xx on analytics endpoints or >5% latency regression sustained for 1 hour.
- Post-rollout: run a purple-team review to attempt to access denied dimensions and produce a short incident playbook if leaks found.
